title: Frozen estimator and three pre-registered replication questions for the next two sessions
rationale: A validated estimator and a pre-registered interpretation now exist. The purpose of the next two sessions is REPLICATION, not estimator development. Freezing every analysis choice before looking at the data is what keeps the three questions below answerable rather than post-hoc.

sessions.role: same subject; trial-identity collision stress test
different subject; strongest identity-repair stress case

frozen_analysis_choices.estimator: nested CV, RidgeCV LOO-GCV inside each training fold, M2 and M3 tuned independently
frozen_analysis_choices.alpha_grid: logspace(-2, 4, 13) -- IDENTICAL to the pilot for replication comparability; boundary hits are LOGGED, not fixed. ~10% of pilot cells saturated the 1e4 ceiling; changing the grid now would break comparability, so the ceiling stays and its hit rate is reported.
frozen_analysis_choices.null_criterion: permuted-arm q95 within trial-count stratum; detection = pooled delta exceeds that floor
frozen_analysis_choices.injection_sensitivity: same beta sweep (0, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4), same equal-weight geometry
frozen_analysis_choices.high_gamma_primary: C1_own_excluded is the PRIMARY high-gamma estimate. C0_own is retained explicitly as a contamination-sensitive comparison, not as the estimate.
frozen_analysis_choices.class_definitions: unchanged; O+/O++ from template-correlation tables joined on unit_row_idx
frozen_analysis_choices.bands: theta, alpha, beta, low_gamma, high_gamma -- unchanged
frozen_analysis_choices.no_new_thresholds: No threshold, band, lag geometry, or model class may be introduced based on anything sub-V182o_ses-260702 showed.

explicitly_not_doing: adding lag geometries -- independent verification showed the four lag predictors are too correlated for geometry to matter, so exploring geometries now would only add researcher degrees of freedom

Q1.question: Does the high-n detection excess recur (pilot: 13.2% against a 5.0% null floor)?
Q1.status_of_pilot_observation: DESCRIPTIVE_REPLICATION_TARGET -- not a finding. It survived a residual-permutation null and a nonlinear-spike-history null (both <=5%) and was distributed across 39/40 units, so it is not a trivial permutation artifact; but n_sessions = 1 forecloses any population inference.
Q1.prespecified_answer_rule: Report the high-n detection rate against each session's OWN permuted floor. Recurrence means a rate materially above 5% in both new sessions. Report it per session; do not pool across sessions to manufacture significance.

Q2.question: Does any omission effect emerge after its own null correction?
Q2.pilot_result: No. The apparent omission deficit under fixed alpha was a trial-count artifact; it vanished after subtracting each cell's own permuted floor, and paired unit-level tests were null (p = 0.37 / 0.74 / 0.95).
Q2.prespecified_answer_rule: Compute nested minus permuted per cell, aggregate to one value per unit, test paired against the matched-empty comparator. Report the sensitivity bound alongside, since the omission conditions are expected to be underpowered again.

Q3.question: Does the high-gamma C0 > C1 discordance recur (pilot: 22.5% vs 17.0%, 14 vs 3 discordant pairs, exact McNemar p = 0.0127)?
Q3.why_it_matters: Same-electrode spike remnants can produce spurious spike-LFP relationships, most acutely in gamma/high-gamma, and the affected frequency range is dataset-specific -- so contamination must be assessed per corpus rather than assumed absent.
Q3.prespecified_answer_rule: Paired C0 vs C1 within (unit, condition), exact McNemar on detections, plus the paired Wilcoxon on deltas to separate a tail effect from a location shift -- exactly as computed in the pilot.

falsifier: This plan closes when both sessions have been run under the frozen configuration and Q1, Q2 and Q3 each have a per-session answer with its receipt.

decision_rule_after_replication.coherent_structure: If the two sessions reproduce a coherent structure, THEN design the session-level corpus analysis.
decision_rule_after_replication.strong_disagreement: If they disagree strongly, diagnose heterogeneity BEFORE scaling. Do not average over a disagreement.
decision_rule_after_replication.binding_constraint: Any corpus-scaling decision is governed by omission-condition trial counts, which are the binding constraint on sensitivity -- not by adding bands, controls, or units.

known_blocker_found_while_freezing.what: The unit-classification table the pilot consumed (omission/artifacts/data/pilot_v182o_260702_unitclass.csv) has NO script in the repo that builds it. It was produced ad hoc in an earlier session.
known_blocker_found_while_freezing.consequence: Replication is impossible until the recipe is reconstructed, because the two new sessions need the same table built the same way.
known_blocker_found_while_freezing.resolution_rule: Reconstruct the builder and validate it by reproducing the EXISTING 260702 table exactly. Bit-identical reproduction is the acceptance test; anything less means the recipe is not recovered and the replication is not comparable.
known_blocker_found_while_freezing.note: This is a reproducibility defect in the pilot, discovered while freezing, and is recorded rather than quietly fixed.
